_notes: Locally added -- upstream pinmame-nvram-maps has no map for NBA.
Built from a 4-player game driven through the cabinet's own streamer.
current_player and current_ball are adjacent in CPU RAM at 0x00033020 and 0x00033021, player low
and ball high. Scores are 4 bytes on 8-byte centres from 0x021109E4.
Nine records from 0x021029F8, bounded by where the 16-bit checksum stops validating -- the tenth
does not pass. Five are the high score ladder; four are champions, named off the machine's
post-game DMD cycle and each pinned by a distinct factory default: Free Throws 2 in a row,
2-Pointers 4, 3-Pointers 3, NBA Finals 25,000,000.
The machine displays a Basketball Points champion, and it is deliberately not mapped: it does not
appear to be stored as a champion record at all. Earning it (6 points) and exiting changed nothing
in the record block, put no 6 anywhere in the persistent region, and left record ten still failing
its checksum. Every persistent byte that did change has the audit shape -- a value written twice
followed by a checksum byte -- and the only 6s are in the volatile working area at 0x02111Axx,
among values that move by millions between captures. It reads as a per-game statistic the
game-over summary shows, not a persisted champion.
Score slots confirmed on that game: 1,336,840 for player 1 at 0x021109E4.
Only nba_802 is claimed; SAM addresses move between revisions.
game_over, tilted and credits come from a 1,099-frame recording of live memory spanning an
indices 30 and 32 as the free_play-relative rule predicted.
This ROM does not keep the ball+0x31 status byte its siblings use (a constant 0 here). Its game
state lives in a block at the top of RAM, 0x0003FF00-0x0003FFFF.
game_over at 0x0003FF83 reads 1 in the attract on both sides of the game and 0 in play, dropping
at the exact frame the game started -- the same frame credits fell -- and returning on the
frame of the last score change (the end-of-ball bonus). Correct in all 1,099 frames; any
non-zero value is game over, so no mask is needed. Ten neighbouring bytes carry the same edges.
tilted at 0x0003FF6B reads 4 for exactly the sixteen samples from the tilt to the end of the
tilted ball -- during which player 1's score sat frozen at 5,250 -- and 0 everywhere else in the
recording. Any non-zero value is tilted.
credits at 0x0211100C, the fourteenth SAM game at that address: rose to 9 with the coins (capped
by the Maximum Credits just set) and fell to 8 at game start.
2026-11: game_over and tilted read the status byte 0x00033052 (player + 0x32; 01 attract, 26
ball served, 12 play, 2F/66 modes, 14 tilted). On a cabinet the previous game_over 0x0003FF83
read game over for 6 s after the tilted ball drained, and tilted 0x0003FF6B went to 4 at each
ball launch, never at the tilt.
2026-11: The A.1 (63) and A.2 (33) adjustments added from the ROM image (README, 'Adjustments
from the ROM').
Confirmed on a cabinet 2026-11-13 (ALP4K; two players, tilt on P1 ball 1): 1,219,840 /
1,045,260, the records and the status byte matched the DMD.
